title: Past actions: what happened and what was in progress

sections.title: Past Simple or Past Continuous?
sections.content:
Use Past Continuous for a background action in progress: I was driving home. Use Past Simple for a completed action: The phone rang. Together: I was driving home when the phone rang.

Türkçe ipucu: devam eden eylem için was/were + -ing; kısa, biten olay için Past Simple kullan. when genellikle kısa olayı, while devam eden eylemi bağlar.

questions.prompt: I ___ dinner when the phone rang.
While they ___ home, it started to rain.
The lights went out while we ___ a film.
Which sentence describes a finished action?
Choose the best pair: “I ___ my keys while I ___ for the bus.”

sections.title: Story-building words
sections.content:
Use suddenly for an unexpected event, meanwhile for a second action at the same time, and eventually for the final result. Example: “I was waiting for the bus. Meanwhile, my friend was looking for a café. Suddenly, it began to rain. Eventually, we found shelter.”

Say each word, then make one true sentence about your own week.

questions.prompt: Which word introduces an unexpected event?
Which word means ‘at the same time’?
Which sentence uses eventually correctly?
choices: Eventually, I was cooking at six.
Eventually, the phone rang while I slept.
Eventually, we arrived after a long journey.

questions.prompt: Choose the best connector: “I was studying. ___, my brother was watching television.”

sections.title: A small interruption
sections.content:
Read: “At 6:15, Arda was walking to the station. He was listening to a podcast and checking the time. Suddenly, he saw that he had left his ticket at home. He ran back, found it on the table, and caught the next train. He arrived ten minutes late, but his colleague was still waiting.”

First, underline the actions in progress. Then circle the short events that changed the story.

questions.prompt: What was Arda doing at 6:15?
choices: He was walking to the station.
He was waiting for a colleague.

questions.prompt: What problem did Arda notice?
choices: He had left his ticket at home.

questions.prompt: What did Arda do after he noticed the problem?
Which statement is true at the end?

sections.title: Listen for the interruption
sections.content:
Ask a study partner or your device’s read-aloud tool to read this twice. First time: listen for the main idea. Second time: listen for the two actions. “Leyla was preparing a presentation when her laptop stopped working. She called a friend, and together they found a copy of the file in her email. Later, Leyla gave the presentation successfully.”

Pause after each sentence and repeat it with clear stress on was preparing, stopped, called, and found.

questions.prompt: What was Leyla doing when the problem happened?
What stopped working?
Where did Leyla find a copy of the file?

sections.title: Tell a short story
sections.content:
Speak for one minute. Use this frame: 1) “Yesterday, I was …” 2) “Then / suddenly, … happened.” 3) “After that, I …”

Example: “Yesterday, I was leaving work when I met a colleague. We talked for a few minutes. After that, I took the bus home.” Record yourself if you can, then listen once and check: Did you use was/were + -ing? Did you include one finished Past Simple action?

sections.title: Final mixed challenge
sections.content: Before choosing, say the full sentence aloud. For a final written challenge, write four sentences about a real interruption: one background action, one short event, one response, and one final result.

questions.prompt: Choose the natural sentence.
choices: I was sleeping when the alarm rang.
I sleeping when the alarm was ring.
I was sleep when the alarm rang.
I slept when the alarm was ringing.

questions.prompt: Complete: “While I ___ for the doctor, I read a magazine.”
Choose the best ending: “The children were playing outside when …”
Which question is correct?
choices: What you were doing at eight?
What did you doing at eight?
What were you do at eight?
What were you doing at eight?

questions.prompt: Choose the clearest story order.
